channel.title: Tammy Journal
channel.description: Australian small-business accounting, pricing, cash-flow and invoicing notes.

item.title: The BAS quarter has two clocks.
item.description: How an invoice dated in June and paid in July places $100 GST into different quarters under cash versus non-cash reporting.

item.title: Not every bank deposit is sales.
item.description: A $8,700 receipt set is only $2,000 of taxable sales ex GST; the remainder is GST, a loan and owner capital.

item.title: The month-end close that found $220.
item.description: A $220 duplicate payment explains a difference between the closing bank statement and ledger; includes a working review checklist.

item.title: The price rise that didn't fix the margin.
item.description: Why a $10 rise in variable cost moves break-even volume from 75 to 100 units in a transparent pricing example.

item.title: The ageing report is using the wrong clock.
item.description: An overdue-invoice ageing example that distinguishes the due date from the issue date and groups $7,100 in receivables.

item.title: When profit and cash part ways.
item.description: An $8,000 accrual-profit and $5,000 net-cash example that reconciles unpaid invoices and bills.

item.title: When GST registration becomes necessary.
item.description: The Australian $75,000 GST turnover threshold, projected turnover, the 21-day rule and registration exceptions.

item.title: Keep the evidence behind the entry.
item.description: Retaining business receipts and source records, five-year baseline, exceptions and digital record safeguards.

item.title: Three BAS labels. One clear workpaper.
item.description: Simpler BAS G1 total sales, 1A GST on sales and 1B eligible GST credits with a worked example.

item.title: Make the bank and ledger agree.
item.description: Trace statement rows, resolve unexplained differences, and retain a verifiable reconciliation.

item.title: Margin is not markup.
item.description: The difference between gross margin and markup, with a concrete Australian small-business break-even example.

item.title: An invoice is not cash.
item.description: Issue date, due date and actual cash receipts are different events. A practical guide to payment terms.

item.title: See the next twelve weeks.
item.description: Build a weekly cash-flow view with opening balance, receipts, payments and closing cash.
